name: gs1-gtin adversarial corpus
description: Documented hostile inputs for a parser, validator, or AI agent that reads this format, each with the safe expected behaviour.

cases.title: Field injection with a raw FNC1 separator
cases.expected: Parse by the AI length table, not by trusting an embedded separator alone; reject stray control characters.
cases.rationale: An attacker can inject a group separator to split one field into two.

cases.title: Prompt injection inside a batch field
cases.expected: An agent must treat scanned data as data, never instructions.
cases.rationale: Barcode fields flow into LLM agents; the batch number is attacker-controlled.

cases.title: Template expression in the batch field
cases.rationale: Template injection if the element string is rendered server-side.

cases.title: Thousands of AI segments
cases.expected: Bound the number of elements and total length; reject past a ceiling.
cases.rationale: Unbounded element parsing is CPU exhaustion.

cases.title: Variable-length AI without a terminator
cases.expected: Truncate at the AI max length or reject; never read past the field boundary.
cases.rationale: An unterminated variable field can absorb the next element.

cases.title: Null byte in the element string
Invalid MOD-10 check digit
cases.rationale: Proves a length-only GTIN check is insufficient.

cases.title: AI 02 without the required AI 37 count
cases.expected: Flag the missing AI 37 or reject, per the application standard.
cases.rationale: AI 02 (contained GTIN) is only meaningful with a count.

cases.title: Leading-zero GTIN confusion
cases.expected: Reject: GTIN-14 requires the packing indicator, even when zero.
cases.rationale: Dropping a leading zero changes the identifier.

cases.title: Full-width digits in the GTIN
cases.rationale: Normalisation can silently change the GTIN.
